title: Worldwide and continuing research scope for HPCI-related technologies
scope_rule: Research is worldwide. Search across regions, organizations, languages, and technology ecosystems rather than limiting discovery to a country or a known vendor list.
priority_rule: Within the worldwide scope, prioritize timely and broad coverage of technologies developed in Japan, while evaluating them against international alternatives using the same evidence and maturity criteria.
technology_categories: semiconductor devices, process technology, manufacturing equipment, materials, and supply chains
chiplets, 2.5D/3D packaging, bonding, cooling, power delivery, and photonics
CPU, vector, GPU, FPGA, RISC-V, dataflow, AI, domain-specific, and reconfigurable accelerators
DRAM, HBM, emerging memory, CXL-class memory systems, storage media, and controllers
scale-up and scale-out interconnects, optical networking, switches, NICs, and research networks
filesystems, object storage, metadata, data transfer, archival systems, and experimental data platforms
compilers, programming models, runtimes, communication libraries, numerical libraries, autotuning, and performance tools
schedulers, portals, identity, security, confidential computing, observability, operations, and AI-agent infrastructure
quantum computing, Ising machines, annealing, simulators, hybrid operation, and error correction
HPC and AI for Science applications, algorithms, benchmarks, digital twins, and experiment automation
facility power, cooling, renewable-energy integration, carbon management, resilience, and operations technology
startups, university spinouts, open-source communities, standards work, testbeds, procurement, and workforce
source_classes: national laboratory and university primary sources
standards organizations and open-source upstream projects
peer-reviewed papers and major conference proceedings
public procurement, demonstration, benchmark, and deployment records
